title: Trees and Selection
summary: A scene hierarchy, a file browser and an asset list all need a tree and a selection that behaves like every other program - click to select, Ctrl+click to add, Shift+click for a range. This lesson covers `TreeNode` and its flags, building a tree from your data, and implementing multi-selection properly.
markdown:
## Tree nodes

```cpp-norun
if (ImGui::TreeNode("Level"))            // true while open
{
    ImGui::Text("child item");
    if (ImGui::TreeNode("Props")) { ImGui::Text("rock"); ImGui::TreePop(); }
    ImGui::TreePop();                    // only if TreeNode returned true
}
```

ImGui remembers whether each node is open by its ID (lesson 1.05), so two nodes with the same label in the same place open and close together. In a loop, use `PushID` or the `TreeNode(ptr_id, fmt, ...)` overload, which takes a pointer as the ID and a separate display text.

## TreeNodeEx and its flags

```cpp-norun
ImGuiTreeNodeFlags flags = ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnArrow       // click the arrow to open, the label to select
                         | ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnDoubleClick
                         | ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_SpanAvailWidth;   // the whole row is clickable
if (node.children.empty()) flags |= ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Leaf | ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_NoTreePushOnOpen;
if (isSelected(node.id))  flags |= ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Selected;

const bool open = ImGui::TreeNodeEx((void*)(intptr_t)node.id, flags, "%s", node.name.c_str());
if (ImGui::IsItemClicked() && !ImGui::IsItemToggledOpen())   // clicked the label, not the arrow
    select(node.id);
```

- `Leaf` draws no arrow; with `NoTreePushOnOpen` you also skip `TreePop` for it.
- `DefaultOpen` opens a node the first time it is seen.
- `ImGui::SetNextItemOpen(true)` opens the next node from code: "reveal the selected object in the tree".

## Building a tree from your data

Scene data is usually a flat list where each object knows its parent. Draw it recursively:

```cpp-norun
void drawNode(const Scene& scene, int id)
{
    const Object& o = scene.objects[id];
    ImGuiTreeNodeFlags flags = ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnArrow | ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_SpanAvailWidth;
    if (o.children.empty()) flags |= ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_Leaf | ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_NoTreePushOnOpen;
    const bool open = ImGui::TreeNodeEx((void*)(intptr_t)id, flags, "%s", o.name.c_str());
    if (open && !o.children.empty())
    {
        for (int child : o.children) drawNode(scene, child);
        ImGui::TreePop();
    }
}
```

The practice builds the "children of each node" lists from parent links and produces the order rows appear in, which is also what Shift+click ranges need.

## Selection that behaves

Users expect:

| Action | Result |
|---|---|
| Click | Select only this item; it becomes the **anchor** |
| Ctrl+click | Toggle this item, keep the others; it becomes the anchor |
| Shift+click | Select every item **between the anchor and this one**, in display order, replacing the selection |
| Ctrl+Shift+click | Add that range to the existing selection |

The **anchor** is the last item clicked without Shift. Ranges are measured in **display order**: the order rows appear on screen, which for a tree is depth-first over the open nodes. Store the selection as a set of stable IDs, never as row positions, so it survives sorting and filtering.

Dear ImGui 1.91 added a full multi-select API (`BeginMultiSelect`/`EndMultiSelect`) that handles these rules, box-selection and keyboard navigation for you; writing the rules yourself once, as the practice does, makes it much easier to use well.

## Common mistakes

> [!warning] Selecting when the arrow was clicked
> Check IsItemToggledOpen so opening a node does not also select it.

> [!warning] Storing the selection as row numbers
> Rows change when the list is sorted, filtered or a node opens. Store IDs.

## Check yourself
```quiz
? What are the Leaf and NoTreePushOnOpen flags for?
- Leaf keeps a node always open; NoTreePushOnOpen stops it being selected
+ Leaf draws a node without an arrow for items with no children; NoTreePushOnOpen means TreePop must not be called for it
- Leaf hides the node's label; NoTreePushOnOpen makes it open on a double click
> With NoTreePushOnOpen the node does not push onto the tree stack when open, so there is nothing to pop.

? What is the anchor in multi-selection?
- The first item in the list, where every Shift+click range starts
- The item under the mouse when the button was pressed
+ The last item clicked without Shift; Shift+click selects from it to the clicked item in display order
> A plain click or a Ctrl+click moves the anchor; a Shift+click does not.

? How do you open a tree node from code to reveal a selected object?
+ Call SetNextItemOpen(true) before drawing each of its ancestors
- Add ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_DefaultOpen to the selected object's node
- Call TreePush with the object's ID after drawing the tree
> Every ancestor must be open for the object to appear. DefaultOpen only applies the first time a node is seen.

? What does ImGuiTreeNodeFlags_OpenOnArrow change?
+ Only clicking the arrow opens the node, so clicking the label can select it
- The node is always open and has no arrow
- The node opens when the mouse hovers over its arrow
> It separates opening from selecting; check IsItemToggledOpen so the arrow click does not also select.

? The anchor is item 3 and the user Shift+clicks item 7. What is selected?
- Only item 7, replacing the previous selection
- Items 3 and 7, added to the previous selection
+ Items 3 to 7, replacing the previous selection
> Shift+click selects the range from the anchor in display order; Ctrl+Shift+click would add it to the existing selection instead.

? Why store selected items by ID rather than by row number?
- IDs take less memory than row numbers do in a set
+ Rows change with sorting, filtering and opening nodes; IDs do not
- ImGui's TreeNodeEx only accepts IDs, never row numbers
> The selection must survive changes to what is shown.
```
ideas:
- Draw your game's scene objects as a tree from parent links, with leaves and selection highlighting.
- Implement click, Ctrl+click and Shift+click selection, then sort or filter the list and check the selection stays correct.
